# Deploying

<!-- generated by `python -m quality.sdk --reference`; edit the source, never this -->

From a pushed main to the product's staging host, in the order you do it. The runbook (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md`) is the operator's book; this page is the order, and links each Part by its anchor.

## 1 · What the account owner runs once

The product's repository exists on GitHub before the bootstrap runs: the bootstrap reads `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>` for the OIDC trust's ids, and on a 404 its plan prints REFUSED and `--confirm` makes nothing (`deploy/iam/product_bootstrap.sh:143`).

A product gets one box per environment, with RDS (Postgres), S3, Secrets Manager, ECR and Route 53 around it. Re-price it before anything is made (step 5 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:177`); `infra` prints what it would create (step 21 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:834`).

How much that box carries, and the shape to move to when an alert says it ran out: [the capacity runbook's shapes](../runbooks/capacity.md#10--shapes--what-each-deployment-shape-carries-what-says-it-ran-out-and-the-move) (`docs/runbooks/capacity.md:748`).

The account owner supplies, once:

- [ ] the namespace, one slug with no default (step 4 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:161`): `export DJB_DEPLOY_NAMESPACE=<ns>`
- [ ] the region: `export AWS_REGION=<region>`
- [ ] the environment (step 3 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:152`): `export DJB_ENV=staging`
- [ ] the Route 53 hosted zone and the domain under it (step 16 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:525`, step 26 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:879`): `export DJB_ZONE_ID=<zone id>` and `export DJB_DOMAIN=<your domain>` — the DOMAIN, not the host: the site is `$DJB_ENV.<DJB_DOMAIN>`, with `auth.` and `o11y.` before it (`deploy/provision.sh:993`)
- [ ] the e-mail address `CADDY_TLS` names (step 32 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1075`): the Let's Encrypt account that certificate expiry notices reach, an address a human reads, named by the account owner
- the first sign-in at the staging host is not the account owner's: it is the deploying developer's, the first admin `zitadel_first_admin` invites by the link it prints (`apps/accounts/management/commands/zitadel_first_admin.py:121`; § 4)
- [ ] the one address ssh admits, this machine's (step 20 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:825`): `export DJB_OWNER_IP="$(curl -s https://checkip.amazonaws.com | tr -d '\n')"`
- [ ] the EC2 key pair — the bootstrap holds no private key (step 18 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:541`)
- [ ] the IAM and the registry, one command — bare, it prints the plan and makes nothing; with `--confirm` it makes it:

```bash
DJB_DEPLOY_NAMESPACE=<ns> AWS_REGION=<region> DJB_ENV=staging DJB_GITHUB_REPO=<owner>/<repo> ./deploy/iam/product_bootstrap.sh
DJB_DEPLOY_NAMESPACE=<ns> AWS_REGION=<region> DJB_ENV=staging DJB_GITHUB_REPO=<owner>/<repo> ./deploy/iam/product_bootstrap.sh --confirm
```

It makes the box's role and instance profile, the three image repositories (`deploy/provision.sh:336`), the GitHub OIDC provider and CI's push and deploy roles (`deploy/iam/product_bootstrap.sh:31`) — in place of step 19 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:552` and step 19a at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:610`. It ends by printing `export DJB_INSTANCE_PROFILE=…` and the variable lines of § 2.

The two CI roles trust both spellings of the repository's OIDC subject, `repo:<owner>/<repo>:…` and `repo:<owner>@<owner id>/<repo>@<repo id>:…`, the ids read with `gh` when the plan prints; which one a repository's tokens carry is `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/oidc/customization/sub`. Re-run with `--confirm` and a role made before both gains the missing subjects (`deploy/iam/product_bootstrap.sh:135`).

next: the repository's variables.

## 2 · The repository's variables

Paste the lines the bootstrap printed, on the product's repository — variables, not secrets:

```bash
gh variable set AWS_ECR_ROLE_ARN --repo <owner>/<repo> --body <as printed>
gh variable set DJB_IMAGE_REGISTRY --repo <owner>/<repo> --body <as printed>
gh variable set AWS_REGION --repo <owner>/<repo> --body <as printed>
gh variable set DJB_DEPLOY_NAMESPACE --repo <owner>/<repo> --body <as printed>
```

With them, every merge to main builds the three images (`deploy/provision.sh:336`) and pushes them to ECR (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1593`).

Leave two unset: `AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN` and `DJB_STAGE_TARGET`. They arm the staging deploy job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:1745`), which reaches the box over plain ssh, and a hosted runner holds no key for it: unset, the job skips with a notice; set, it is red on the ssh refusal. Why: [Deploying from CI — the two jobs, and the transport a product builds](../runbooks/deploy.md#deploying-from-ci--the-two-jobs-and-the-transport-a-product-builds) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1604`).

The stack's registry is the product's choice (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:716`): `DJB_STACK_REGISTRY`, an optional variable, names the product's own mirror if it runs one; else the repository SECRETS `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`/`DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` log the pull in to Docker Hub; else it is anonymous, and Docker Hub rate-limits a full matrix.

next: the first deploy.

## 3 · The deploy, and how to watch it

The first deploy is the runbook's hand walk, from your checkout, the Parts in order:

0. Preflight (step 0 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:201`): `./deploy/provision.sh preflight <env>` reads every precondition of the walk below — the env file's slots, the key pair, the bucket names, the box role's `djb-box`, the images, the secret, the zone — and writes nothing; one line per check names its step and the fix. Exit 0 ok · 1 refused · 2 could not look (`deploy/provision.sh:1990`). Run it again after every take. The one check the laptop cannot make is the box's own `docker login`, and its line says so: `preflight <env> --on-box`, run on the box, asks the registry as the box (`deploy/provision.sh:1957`).
1. [Part 0 · Before you start](../runbooks/deploy.md#part-0--before-you-start) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:133`) — the tools, the environment, the namespace, the price.
2. [Part 1 · The laptop proof](../runbooks/deploy.md#part-1--the-laptop-proof) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:199`) — the whole stack on your laptop, no AWS: prove `deploy/` before you pay for it.
3. [Part 2 · Provision](../runbooks/deploy.md#part-2--provision) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:523`) — `provision.sh env-file`, `secrets-put`, then `infra --confirm`. RDS takes minutes: step 23 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:847` waits for its endpoint and step 24 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:855` re-stores the environment with it.
4. [Part 3 · DNS and the box](../runbooks/deploy.md#part-3--dns-and-the-box) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:877`) — the three names at the box, docker on it, `ship.sh` sends the tree and writes the box's `TREE` marker, the environment from Secrets Manager.
5. [Part 4 · Deploy](../runbooks/deploy.md#part-4--deploy) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1046`) — the image for this tree must already be in ECR (the merge pushed it), and the box's daemon logged in to it before `image-digest` asks (step 33 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1090`): `aws ecr get-login-password --region <region> | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <registry host>`; `provision.sh up`; Caddy's certificates wait on Part 3's names.
6. [Part 5 · Release](../runbooks/deploy.md#part-5--release) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1227`) — `release.sh`: the migration and the release SQL.
7. [Part 6 · Identity](../runbooks/deploy.md#part-6--identity) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1459`) — the PAT, `zitadel_seed`, the workforce provider; then § 4. The audience step 42 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1484` sets is the project id, which the seed prints as `ZITADEL_MCP_AUDIENCE=<project id>` (`apps/accounts/management/commands/zitadel_seed.py:211`).
8. [Part 7 · Smoke](../runbooks/deploy.md#part-7--smoke) (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1570`) — § 6.

Staging sends no e-mail until a provider key is set: `env-file` leaves `ANYMAIL_RESEND_API_KEY` empty by design (`deploy/provision.sh:912`), so the first send logs `comms.message.failed` with `AnymailConfigurationError`. That is the expected outcome until the key is set, and preflight says so on its step-24 line, naming `deploy.md § Email mechanism` (`docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1796`), the page that owns every provider's key.

Every deploy after the first is one command, from a clean checkout at the tree you want live:

```bash
./deploy/stage.sh <user>@<host> --env staging --dry-run
./deploy/stage.sh <user>@<host> --env staging
```

The first cannot be `stage.sh`: it reads the box's `TREE` marker before it decides anything and refuses a box with none, and it re-deploys onto the box, DNS and vault Parts 2–3 made (`deploy/stage.sh:38`).

Watch it: `stage.sh` prints each act's seconds and ends `stage: <tag> live in <n>s (migrate <m>s)` (`deploy/stage.sh:91`); exit 0 live · 1 an act failed · 2 refused, nothing touched. The images: `gh run watch` on the merge's run.

next: the first human.

## 4 · The first human and the first tenant

On the box, in the tree `ship.sh` landed, after Part 6's steps 41–45. In this order:

1. Invite the first human — it prints a link once, where that person sets their own password (`apps/accounts/management/commands/zitadel_first_admin.py:1`):

   ```bash
   docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml run --rm -T oneoff python manage.py zitadel_first_admin --email you@yourcompany.com
   ```

2. That person signs in once at `https://<host>/accounts/login/` — the sign-in is what makes their user.
3. The first tenant, with them as its owner (step 46 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1531`):

   ```bash
   docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml run --rm -T oneoff python manage.py bootstrap_tenant --email you@yourcompany.com --name "Your Company" --slug yourco
   ```

A deployment that federates at birth skips step 1: the first sign-in through the workforce provider makes the user. Both commands refuse once a tenant exists; from then on people arrive by [`pilecap.tenancy.invite_member`](pilecap.tenancy.md#pilecaptenancyinvite_member).

next: each tenant's setup.

## 5 · Each tenant's own setup

Per tenant, through the doors — the SDK pages say how:

- a comms template: [`pilecap.comms.create_template`](pilecap.comms.md#pilecapcommscreate_template)
- a webhook-in endpoint's secret — the connection is the endpoint: [`pilecap.connections.create_connection`](pilecap.connections.md#pilecapconnectionscreate_connection), [`pilecap.connections.update_credentials`](pilecap.connections.md#pilecapconnectionsupdate_credentials); the shape: [`webhook-in`](shapes.md). A new connection accepts only `X-Signature-V2` deliveries; pass `is_signature_v2_required=False` for a provider that cannot timestamp a request
- an outbound endpoint's signing key: [`pilecap.events.issue_endpoint_secret`](pilecap.events.md#pilecapeventsissue_endpoint_secret)

next: the smoke.

## 6 · The smoke

- ready, from outside, over real TLS (step 47 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1572`):

  ```bash
  curl -s https://<host>/readyz
  ```

- the doors against the live host (step 50 at `docs/runbooks/deploy.md:1592`): a token minted on the box, then REST and `/mcp` with it. `feature.sh --drive` mints its token in this checkout's database, so it drives your laptop, never the host:

  ```bash
  docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml run --rm -T oneoff python manage.py issue_token --email you@yourcompany.com --tenant yourco --name smoke --scope <family>:read --scope runs:read
  export TOKEN=<the token it printed>
  curl -s https://<host>/api/v1/<prefix>/ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  ```

- the worker — the deployed stack runs no Temporal UI; the run door is the window (`apps/workflows/api.py:54`), and a run that never closes is a rule-28 finding:

  ```bash
  curl -s https://<host>/api/v1/runs/ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  docker compose -f deploy/compose.yaml logs worker --tail 50
  ```
